factor_name: Ball - 2016 - Accruals, cash flows, and operating profitability in the cross section of stock returns
paper_ref: Ball, Ray, Joseph Gerakos, Juhani T. Linnainmaa, and Valeri Nikolaev, 2016, Journal of Financial Economics 121, 28-45.
economic_intuition: Cash-based operating profitability removes accrual adjustments from operating profitability, and the paper argues that the cash-based component is the part that predicts the cross section of expected returns.
detailed_definition: Operating profitability purged of accrual-related working-capital adjustments, scaled by lagged book value of total assets.

source_details: balance sheet items used for accrual adjustments
book value of total assets lagged by one year

required_fields.concept: Monthly stock return used in portfolio returns and factor construction.
Delisting return used when available and for performance-related delisting imputation logic.
Indicator of whether a delisting is performance-related for delisting return imputation.
Market capitalization used for sample inclusion, microcap split, and size sorts.
Book-to-market control and sample inclusion variable.
Sample inclusion variable required by the paper's sample construction.
Book value of total assets used as lagged scaling denominator.
Revenue input to operating profitability.
Cost of goods sold input to operating profitability.
Reported sales, general, and administrative expenses input to operating profitability.
required_fields.source_detail: Reported sales, general, and administrative expenses

required_fields.concept: Research and development expenditure added back to undo the adjustment embedded in XSGA.
Accounts receivable used in cash-basis adjustment.
Inventory used in cash-basis adjustment.
Prepaid expenses used in cash-basis adjustment.
Current deferred revenue component used in cash-basis adjustment.
Long-term deferred revenue component used in cash-basis adjustment.
Trade accounts payable used in cash-basis adjustment.
Accrued expenses used in cash-basis adjustment.
Prior one-year return used as control and sample inclusion variable.
required_fields.source_detail: returns for the prior one-year period

required_fields.concept: Current month return used as control and sample inclusion variable.
Paper-level concept used to restrict the sample to ordinary common shares traded on NYSE, Amex, and Nasdaq.
required_fields.source_detail: all firms traded on NYSE, Amex, and Nasdaq, and exclude securities other than ordinary common shares

required_fields.concept: Industry code used to exclude financial firms with one-digit SIC code of six.
Signal variable used in the second independent sort of the factor construction.

formula.expression: (revt_t - cogs_t - (xsga_t - xrd_t) - delta(rect,1)_t - delta(invt,1)_t - delta(xpp,1)_t + delta(drc_drlt,1)_t + delta(ap,1)_t + delta(xacc,1)_t) / at_t_minus_1
formula.paper_expression: Cash-based operating profitability = Operating profitability - Δ(Accounts receivable) - Δ(Inventory) - Δ(Prepaid expenses) + Δ(Deferred revenue) + Δ(Trade accounts payable) + Δ(Accrued expenses), with all variables deflated by the book value of total assets in year t-1.

evidence.quote: Cash-based operating profitability = Operating profitability − Δ(Accounts receivable (RECT)) − Δ(Inventory (INVT)) − Δ(Prepaid expenses (XPP)) + Δ(Deferred revenue (DRC+DRLT)) + Δ(Trade accounts payable (AP)) + Δ(Accrued expenses (XACC))
evidence.interpretation: The appendix gives the paper's explicit formula for the signal numerator and the relevant balance-sheet components.

evidence.quote: lag annual accounting information by six months
evidence.interpretation: This establishes the six-month accounting lag. The June-end annual rebalance sentence provides the portfolio formation month and ensuing annual holding cycle.

evidence.quote: The sample consists of firms with non-missing
evidence.interpretation: The sample is restricted to firms meeting the stated non-missing conditions. Separately, the appendix explicitly says missing balance-sheet accounts used in the cash-basis adjustment are replaced with zero for signal computation.

portfolio.universe: U.S. ordinary common shares traded on NYSE, Amex, and Nasdaq, excluding financial firms, with the paper's required return/accounting data available.
portfolio.long_leg: average of small-robust and big-robust cash-based operating profitability portfolios
portfolio.short_leg: average of small-weak and big-weak cash-based operating profitability portfolios

implied_factor_direction.long_leg: average of small-robust and big-robust cash-based operating profitability portfolios
implied_factor_direction.short_leg: average of small-weak and big-weak cash-based operating profitability portfolios
implied_factor_direction.note: The factor is explicitly constructed as robust minus weak in the paper.

reported_results.return_horizon: monthly factor returns from annually rebalanced portfolios

comparison_policy.note: The paper defines the factor as robust-minus-weak and reports positive average returns in that direction.

input_return.name: monthly_stock_return
input_return.expression: ret_m_plus_1 adjusted for CRSP delisting returns; if delisting return is missing and performance-related, substitute -0.30 for the delisting return
adjustments: impute -30% when delisting return is missing and the delisting is performance-related

source.quote: Delisting returns are taken from CRSP
source.interpretation: This sentence and the following imputation sentence define the monthly stock return input handling.

sorts.breakpoint: below 30th and above 70th NYSE percentile breakpoints

return_combination.long_leg: average of robust cash-based operating profitability portfolios across small and big size groups
return_combination.short_leg: average of weak cash-based operating profitability portfolios across small and big size groups
return_combination.note: Middle 40% profitability portfolios are not used in the factor spread.

portfolio_return.holding_period: folios are rebalanced annually at the end of June and held for the following year, generating monthly factor returns

source.quote: The cash-based operating profitability factor, RMW CbOP, is constructed in the same way
source.interpretation: The preceding sentences define the six-portfolio methodology and make clear that RMW CbOP uses the same robust-minus-weak averaging construction.
Table 5 reports the cash-based operating profitability factor's average annualized return as 4.88%.
